text: How much EU money in total was committed to Marie Sklodowska-Curie Individual Fellowship grants, counting every action code under which such fellowships are recorded?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(ecMaxContribution) AS total_ec_contribution FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%'

value_note_dependencies: project.fundingScheme value note (schema_docs 'project' section): the 56-value action-type enum lists MSCA-IF and MSCA-IF-EF-ST as separate top values, so the Individual Fellowship action exists in the data as six distinct codes - MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF, MSCA-IF-EF-RI, MSCA-IF-EF-CAR, MSCA-IF-EF-SE - and a family-wide total needs a prefix match, not fundingScheme = 'MSCA-IF'
project.ecMaxContribution value note: committed EU funding for the project, the column to use for 'EU funding' questions (totalCost is not EU funding)

reference_answer: Across every action code under which Individual Fellowships are recorded, the committed EU contribution comes to 1877777635.91 EUR. A total restricted to grants filed under the bare MSCA-IF code would come to only 996501996.78 EUR, because the fellowship's sub-variants are stored as separate fundingScheme values.
notes: Value note relied on: the project.fundingScheme note in schema_docs ('56 values; top: MSCA-IF, RIA, SME-1, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, ...'), which reveals that the Individual Fellowship action is not one value but a family; plus the ecMaxContribution note ('USE THIS for EU funding questions'). Grounded this pass: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*), SUM(ecMaxContribution) FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%' GROUP BY 1 returns 13 MSCA codes, of which exactly six begin with 'MSCA-IF' - MSCA-IF 5037 / 996501996.78, MSCA-IF-EF-ST 3792 / 678648142.54, MSCA-IF-GF 407 / 94800898.58, MSCA-IF-EF-RI 340 / 59553752.75, MSCA-IF-EF-CAR 145 / 26746832.52, MSCA-IF-EF-SE 124 / 21526012.74. No non-IF scheme starts with 'MSCA-IF', so the prefix match is exactly the IF family (9845 projects, 0 null ecMaxContribution). The competing narrow reading (fundingScheme = 'MSCA-IF') returns 5037 projects / 996501996.78 EUR; the question wording forecloses it with 'counting every action code under which such fellowships are recorded', without disclosing how many codes there are or what they are.

text: The European Research Council runs several different kinds of grant. For each ERC grant type in the H2020 data - the funding schemes whose code starts with ERC- - how long does a project last on average, in days from its start date to its end date (end date minus start date)?
gold_sql: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*) AS n_projects, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day', startDate, endDate)),1) AS avg_duration_days FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC-%' GROUP BY fundingScheme ORDER BY fundingScheme
reference_answer: Seven funding schemes carry an ERC- code, and their average durations fall into a long band and a short one. The long band is the main research grants, 5.7 to 6.7 years each: ERC-SyG averages 2446.0 days (99 projects), ERC-COG 2099.9 days (2254), ERC-STG 2083.3 days (2771) and ERC-ADG 2082.5 days (1584). The short band runs from about 1.6 to 1.8 years: ERC-LVG averages 656.2 days (5 projects), ERC-POC-LS 610.4 days (158) and ERC-POC 576.1 days (967). The five ERC-LVG grants are support awards to external publishing initiatives (OAPEN, SciPost, Europe PMC) rather than research projects. No ERC project has a missing start or end date, so all 7838 of them are included.
notes: Group set is pinned in the question text to the ERC- scheme code, and the text also pins the metric to subtraction (end date minus start date), because an inclusive endpoint count returns exactly +1.0 day on all seven rows and results_match compares at 1e-6. Boundedness checked on two channels. (1) Scheme string: SELECT DISTINCT fundingScheme FROM project WHERE lower(fundingScheme) LIKE '%erc%' OR lower(fundingScheme) LIKE '%research council%' returns exactly the seven ERC- codes (ERC-ADG, ERC-COG, ERC-LVG, ERC-POC, ERC-POC-LS, ERC-STG, ERC-SyG). (2) Programme channel, the near-miss: SELECT p.fundingScheme, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('day',p.startDate,p.endDate)),1) FROM project p JOIN legal_basis lb ON lb.projectID=p.id WHERE lower(lb.title) LIKE '%european research council%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 returns those seven rows unchanged PLUS an eighth group, CSA | 12 | 813.1 - ERC administration and communication contracts under the ERC programme part. The question's ERC- clause makes that eight-group reading unavailable. Duration is pinned to whole days deliberately: a months formula has two defensible variants (calendar month-boundary count vs days/30.44) giving different numbers. Null-date exposure is zero: the 12 corpus-wide projects with NULL startDate/endDate (structural finding sf-11) are all outside the ERC schemes - SUM(CASE WHEN startDate IS NULL OR endDate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 for every ERC- scheme, over 7838 ERC projects. ERC-LVG's five members were read directly (637529 ERC-EuropePMC-2-2014, 683680 ERC-OAPEN-2015, 810640 ERC-OAPEN-2017, 899590 ERC-SciPost-2019, 964352 ERC-OAPEN-2019) so the reference describes them from their titles, not by analogy to ERC-POC. Averages rounded to one decimal in the gold SQL. n_projects is context, not compared; answer_columns pins fundingScheme and avg_duration_days. No ranking asked or implied - sql_comparison=set.

text: Among Horizon 2020 projects that started on or after 1 January 2018, how many had at least one Italian organisation receiving more than 1 million euros of EU funding?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.projectID) AS project_count FROM organization o JOIN project p ON p.id = o.projectID WHERE o.country = 'IT' AND o.ecContribution > 1000000 AND p.startDate >= DATE '2018-01-01'
reference_answer: 478 Horizon 2020 projects with a start date on or after 1 January 2018 include at least one Italian-based organisation whose EU contribution exceeds 1,000,000 EUR. Those projects account for 548 such Italian participations, so a count of organisation rows rather than distinct projects overstates the answer as 548.
notes: Trap = entity grain (organization participation rows vs projects). Wrong query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS project_count FROM organization o JOIN project p ON p.id = o.projectID WHERE o.country = 'IT' AND o.ecContribution > 1000000 AND p.startDate >= DATE '2018-01-01' -> 548; gold with COUNT(DISTINCT o.projectID) -> 478. Both executed this pass. Corpus-wide drift check of the seed evidence reproduced: country='IT' gives 17,243 organization rows vs 7,899 distinct projects. organization.ecContribution is NULL for 7,658 unfunded MSCA 'partner' rows plus 142 others; NULL > 1000000 is not true, so unfunded participations are correctly excluded by the threshold. 'started' maps to project.startDate (action start per schema_docs), not ecSignatureDate. Threshold is strict > 1,000,000 EUR. Not a rank question: sql_comparison=set, no ORDER BY.

text: Which project brought historians of philosophy together with theoretical physicists to compare the conceptions of time in Plato and Kant with emergent time in quantum gravity and quantum cosmology?
reference_answer: PROTEUS (project 758145), 'Paradoxes and Metaphors of Time in Early Universe(s)'. It built a multi-disciplinary team of historians of philosophy, philosophers of physics and theoretical physicists to study how Western philosophy represents time in cosmology, examining the notions of time and the paradoxes arising in the philosophy and cosmology of Plato and Kant and setting them against the fundamental characters of emergent time in current quantum gravity and quantum cosmology. Its results include the digital archive 'Timaeus and Its Legacy', the COSMOS Network, and the edited volume 'Time and Timelessness in Fundamental Physics and Cosmology' (Springer 2024).
notes: Seed 758145 (PROTEUS) taken from corpus-profile candidate vector-04; drift check re-ran the candidate SQL (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocTitle='history of philosophy') -> 1, and the single tagged project is 758145. Question composed from the seed's own report text ('historians of philosophy, philosophers of physics and theoretical physicists'; 'the notions of time and the paradoxes emerging in the philosophy and cosmology of Plato and Kant'; 'the fundamental characters of emergent time in current quantum gravity theories'). Pooled search at k=10 returned 20 distinct projects; seed ranked 1 in all four conditions. Adjudications: 758145 IN (text states exactly the philosopher-physicist collaboration on Plato/Kant vs emergent time). OUT: 647272 Perspectival Realism (philosophy of science / perspectivism, Kant only via the 'Copernican Revolution', no quantum gravity time); 725883 EarlyModernCosmology (17th-century confessional cosmology institutions); 655524 FDtoQG, 656491 BRANECOSMOLOGY, 659151 QEAH, 772295 Qosmology, 679278 Emergent-BH, 740209 eQG, 657661 Space-Time from Info, 815673 GRAMS, 101023293 NRST, 646702 CosTesGrav, 660061 NCDIFFGEO (all pure theoretical physics, no history of philosophy); 101022186 GEOCOSM (Kant's political writings), 101027095 DEKANT (Kant on ethics and right), 777786 KANTINSA (Kant scholarship in South America), 885273 PlatoViaAristotle (ancient Platonism), 840765 NeT-HiDeA (time in history/politics, Sartre and Bloch), 757295 FraMEPhys (metaphysical explanation in physics, no Plato/Kant cosmology). Completeness sweep (run_sql, non-embedding): (a) objective ILIKE Plato OR Kant AND (quantum OR cosmolog) -> 5 rows: 758145 plus 647272 (OUT above), 865075 EXACTC (gauge theories/integrability), 892528 ENNSE (17th-century Edinburgh natural philosophy teaching, read in full - OUT), 101033630 newDFT (density functional theory) - all OUT; (b) objective ILIKE 'quantum gravity' OR 'quantum cosmolog' AND (philosoph OR metaphysic) -> only 758145; (c) euroSciVoc 'history of philosophy' -> only 758145. term_style exact-term: the question reuses the gold text's distinctive vocabulary (Plato, Kant, emergent time, quantum gravity, quantum cosmology, historians of philosophy) and the gold ranks 1 under the lexical condition, which is consistent with real term overlap. Level L1 computed from |gold|=1.

text: How is European research trying to replace the traditional remedy for people bitten by poisonous snakes - the kind produced from the blood of animals repeatedly exposed to the poison - with proteins engineered in the laboratory instead?
reference_answer: Two projects pursue laboratory-made replacements for conventional antivenoms, which are derived from immunised animals (ADDovenom notes current products come from hyperimmunised horses and sheep, that only 10-15% of their IgGs bind venom, and that repeat vials raise adverse effects and cost). MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species; it developed and patented a universal pH-switch for antibodies, which resulted in the spinout Y-king Biologics and EUR 3 million in secured funding, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders against snake toxins, published in Nature Communications and Nature. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.
notes: Seeds came from the corpus-profile candidate vector-16 (animal venom in medicine); its fenced SQL re-ran unchanged at 4 rows (655153, 714366, 891733, 949830). Dropping the euroSciVoc bucket fence, as a vector question must, the corpus-wide venom family is 12 projects, inside which the only crisp 2-4 member theme is snakebite therapy: 850974 MABSTER and 899670 ADDovenom. Both IN by full text: MABSTER develops recombinant human monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies and designed minibinders to replace animal-derived antivenom; ADDovenom develops ADDobody/ADDomer synthetic scaffolds as antivenom for Sub-Saharan Africa. Pooled k=10 over all four conditions returned 23 distinct projects; 21 rejected. Notable OUTs: 949830 ToxMim (turns venom toxins INTO drug leads for human disease, does not treat snakebite), 654294 TentaclesOfVenom / 845674 EVER / 101031131 SpecSpiderVenom / 748902 VIPS / 841576 Finding VENomS (venom evolution and biodiscovery, no bite therapy), 728647 SOS Jelly (skin cream against jellyfish stings, not snake bite, not an engineered protein therapy), 891733 MITafterVIT and 655153 IgEPath (allergy/immune response to venom, not a treatment for bite victims), 751567 NATRICINE / 101027605 EARtH / 101024700 HeadStrong / 101030356 Snake-eyes / 703438 Evol-Eyes (snake biology and evolution), plus off-topic protein/blood engineering hits (715207 MMA, 637877 PredicTOOL, 834952 BIOIMPROVE, 669768 VESCEL, 877280 HemaXis DX, 770992 BloodVariome, 675111 EVOluTION, 740189 EuroBioTox) and non-biomedical lexical noise (763285 PAHremov, 644090 EuroCPS, 863503 ECBS, 816553 DEGCAE, 656067 NOVENA, 101038087 SPHEROTOX). Completeness sweep: (a) objective/title ILIKE snakebite|snake bite|antivenom|anti-venom|envenom|serpent + title snake|venom -> 19 rows, only MABSTER and ADDovenom are bite therapy; (b) objective ILIKE snake|scorpion|viper|cobra AND toxin|bite|antibod|therap -> 5 rows, the other three (COBRAIN, MES-CoBraD, OPENCORONA) are substring noise on 'cobra'; (c) lexical search over the chunk corpus (covers report text the objective sweeps miss) for 'antivenom snakebite envenoming treatment for snake bite victims' -> MABSTER rank 1, ADDovenom rank 2, no other therapy project. MABSTER's objective states snakebite envenoming kills more than 100,000 victims a year. Reference attribution checked against MABSTER's workPerformed: the spinout Y-king Biologics and the EUR 3 million belong to the patented universal pH-switch for antibodies (Structural biology section), while the nanobody/minibinder pipeline is the thread published in Nature Communications and Nature. term_style paraphrase: the question says remedy, poisonous snakes, poison, blood of animals repeatedly exposed, proteins engineered in the laboratory, while the gold texts say antivenom, snakebite envenoming, venom toxins, immunized/hyperimmunised horses and sheep, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, ADDomer, phage display, neutralise. The matrix agrees: ADDovenom is invisible to lexical (dense 1, hybrid_rerank 1) and MABSTER is only lexical 5 against dense 2 / hybrid 1.

text: Which projects build a microfluidic chip device that carries a working model of the human blood-brain barrier or neurovascular unit, either as the whole chip or as one compartment of a larger organ-on-chip system?
reference_answer: Thirteen projects put a working blood-brain barrier (BBB) or neurovascular unit (NVU) model inside a microfluidic chip, almost all justified by the failure of animal and static in vitro models to predict human drug transport into the brain. Most build a dedicated BBB/NVU device: NVU-Chip recapitulates the human NVU in a single microfluidic device and is the first to incorporate cyclic mechanical strain in a BBB model; NOVACHIP builds a scalable vessel-like BBB-on-a-chip from bioprinted endothelialized capillaries; NeuroVU adds real-time chemical and trans-endothelial electrical resistance sensing to an NVU Organ-on-Chip; SONGBIRD integrates 3D scaffolds carrying blood-brain barrier cells into a microfluidic barrier-on-chip screening platform; SweetBrain, DIANA and BrainChip4MED use NVU and brain-on-a-chip models for disease-mechanism work and for screening drugs and nanocarriers that must cross the BBB. Others reach the same structure from vascular or microfabrication engineering: VESCEL engineers hiPSC blood vessels in microfluidic chips and applies them on-chip to blood-brain barrier function, 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP's 3D-printed microfluidic devices generate and maintain living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier, BBBhybrid two-photon-prints a 1:1-scale biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip model of the brain tumour microenvironment with its blood neurovasculature, and FEBRIS builds 3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks to study blood-brain-barrier disruption in cerebral malaria. A third group carries the barrier as one compartment of a bigger chip: MINERVA's microbiota-gut-brain organ-on-a-chip platform, whose brain compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model, and GUTVIBRATIONS' stacked gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip with a blood-brain layer.
notes: MEMBERSHIP RULE, stated in the question text so it is derivable without these notes: the project's own text must describe (i) a microfluidic or chip-based device that the project itself builds and (ii) a BBB or NVU model living in it; the device rule is by wording, and a BBB/NVU compartment inside a larger organ-on-chip system counts. Scope chosen because the corpus-wide organ-on-chip family (~60 projects by title/objective) has no enumerable boundary, while the BBB/NVU has a small set of literal names. IN (13): 101038093 NVU-Chip (3D microfluidic human NVU, first cyclic strain in a BBB model); 840626 NOVACHIP (scalable 3D BBB-on-a-chip); 832045 BBBhybrid (biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip of the brain tumour microenvironment, hCMEC/D3 endothelium + astrocytes in a microfluidic device); 757444 SONGBIRD (barrier-on-chip built around blood-brain barrier cells in a microfluidic network); 797777 NeuroVU (NVU Organ-on-Chip with sensors); 851765 SweetBrain (human-relevant NVU-OoC); 899431 DIANA (BBB-brain model Chip4D Brain on patented organ-on-chip technology); 101032481 BrainChip4MED (microfluidic brain-on-a-chip recapitulating brain tissue and BBB); 724734 MINERVA (engineered organ-on-a-chip platform whose Brain-compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model - compartment clause); 953201 GUTVIBRATIONS (gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip whose deliverables include a blood-brain layer - compartment clause); 101026717 FEBRIS (3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks, BBB disruption in cerebral malaria); 669768 VESCEL (blood vessels engineered in microfluidic chips; report sub-aim 6 applies the blood vessels on-chip to blood-brain barrier function); 798014 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP (3D-printed microfluidic devices that, with hydrogel bioprinting, generate and maintain over time living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier). OUT with the separating fact: 948088 Mal3D-BBB builds a 3D BBB model of collagen gel with endothelial cells, pericytes and astrocytes, but zero of its 5 chunks contain microfluidic, chip or microphysiological - no chip device, so it fails clause (i); this is the one project the device rule deliberately excludes and it is named here so the boundary is visible. 807015 IM2PACT (iPSC-derived BBB models, zero chunks mentioning microfluidic or chip); 865176 Ctrl-BBB (BBB molecular biology, no chip text); 794726 EFHHBBBMS (its text names no device it builds - the microfluidic chamber appears as a requirement of models used during a secondment, and the fellowship's stated outputs are biological findings; closest OUT under this rule); 739759 BrainChip, 824070 CONNECT, 743909 NOC, 840984 NMJ, 842423 BrainCircuit-on-chip, 658850 Als-on-a-chip (neural or brain tissue chips with no BBB/NVU model); 101003361 GliomaChip, 835227 3DBrainStrom (brain tumour chips, not barrier models); 727641 BioREAD (electrical barrier-quality detector FOR organs-on-chip, builds no BBB model); 840231 PTOoC, 753743 MOOAC, 795754 MTOAC, 762315 B-On-Chip, 884823 PORTable STaNDOuTs, 897025 open-TOP (generic or other-organ organ-on-chip devices; none carries a BBB/NVU term anywhere in its text); 779751 INVICTUS (vessel-on-a-chip for ultrasound cavitation); 750601 CLIMB (supported lipid membrane permeability assay, no cells, no chip model); 115975 ADAPTED, 813294 ENTRAIN, 798505 NanoBBB, 829040 MindGAP, 804229 LIMBo (BBB biology or nanomaterial transport, no chip model). COMPLETENESS SWEEP, two arms over the chunk table so report text is covered: arm 1 (the rule's own predicate) = projects with a BBB/NVU term (blood-brain barrier, blood brain barrier, blood-brain-barrier, neurovascular unit, standalone BBB, brain endothelial barrier) AND a chip term (microfluidic, on-chip, on a chip, microphysiological) -> 33 projects, every one adjudicated. Arm 2 (falsification arm, no chip term required) = BBB/NVU term AND an engineered-model term (in vitro with 3D, perfus, engineered, recapitulat or tubular) -> 26 projects of which 10 carry no chip term at all: 642028 NABBA, 721975 in3, 758887 REACT, 803621 LINCE, 825161 ATHENA, 828837 GLADIATOR, 897678 NeuroMOF, 898170 PiezoMagBBB, 948088 Mal3D-BBB, 964934 NECTAR; only Mal3D-BBB builds an engineered 3D BBB model, and it is excluded by the device clause as stated above, the other nine being nanomedicine, theranostics or assay projects. term_style exact-term: the question reuses the gold texts' literal vocabulary (microfluidic, chip, organ-on-chip, blood-brain barrier, neurovascular unit); lexical ranked NVU-Chip 1, NeuroVU 2, SweetBrain 4, VESCEL 7, BBBhybrid 9. Seven of the thirteen gold appear in the final pooled top-10 (NVU-Chip, NeuroVU, NOVACHIP, SweetBrain, BrainChip4MED, VESCEL, BBBhybrid); DIANA, SONGBIRD, MINERVA, GUTVIBRATIONS, FEBRIS and 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP were established by reading plus the sweep, not by the pool at k=10.

text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects on nanoscale light control, which one set out to do away with the lenses and reflectors added onto low-energy lamps by placing the light-emitting nanoparticles inside engineered surroundings - stacked layers, patterned surfaces and resonant cavities - so that the tint and the beam spread of the light are fixed by those surroundings rather than by changing what the particles themselves are made of?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/nanophotonics%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG'

reference_answer: NANOPHOM (project 715832) is the ERC Starting Grant in question: it puts rare-earth nanophosphors inside engineered optical structures - multilayers, surface textures, nano-scatterers, nanoimprinted corrugations and optical cavities - and shows that those surroundings alone set the chromaticity and the directionality of the device's output, 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', replacing the reflectors and lenses normally added as secondary optical elements. Its target demonstrations were directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone and omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'nanophotonics' (one-reading check: 'engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nanophotonics' is the only path matching '%nanophotonics%', 62 projects) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-STG' -> 10 survivors, re-executed this pass. Runtime note: the scoped path (src/retrieval/scoped.py) can only filter the structural half ('ERC Starting Grant' -> fundingScheme='ERC-STG'); the nanophotonics topic is carried by retrieval, which is how the question is worded. LOW note on scope width: the enumerated survivor set is narrower than the runtime's executable scope (all ERC-STG projects), so ERC-STG projects tagged under other euroSciVoc leaves - e.g. 849229 CQWLED (nanocrystals / colors / optoelectronics) - are reachable at runtime but not enumerated here; CQWLED is excluded by the question's own words (see ADJUDICATION), so this is a recorded width note, not a gold gap. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 10 survivors read at objective+teaser, gold at full payload; re-adjudicated against the current wording): 715832 NANOPHOM IN - 'exploits new ways of controlling the emission characteristics of nanophosphors, surpassing the limits imposed by conventional optics', design 'based on multilayers, surface textures and nano-scatterers', and the report states the control comes 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', with reflectors and lenses named as the secondary optical elements being replaced. OUT: 637116 ENLIGHTMENT (photonic electrodes to enhance light ABSORPTION in thin solar cells, photodetectors, sensors); 639109 FLATLIGHT (visible-wavelength metasurfaces as ultrathin reconfigurable optical components and modulators, not emission from a lamp's emitting particles); 677470 SEAQUEL (cold structured atomic ensembles for quantum engineering of light); 679841 ORDERin1D (chirality-sorted carbon nanotubes, molecular filling and order); 714151 PSINFONI (particle-surface near-field interactions, optical and Casimir forces); 802682 MODES (nonlinear multimode processes in fibres, chips and nanoparticles); 802986 aQUARiUM (epsilon-near-zero rolled-up metamaterials for quantum light-matter interaction); 853500 NanoGraphy (plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic nanolithography); 948804 CHANSON (chiral semiconductor nanophotonics for molecular sensing). NEAR-MISSES EXCLUDED BY THE QUESTION'S OWN WORDS: 798697 NEXTLEDs is titled 'Chemical Engineering of Atomically-Flat Colloidal Quantum Wells' and works by synthesizing the emitters themselves - the mechanism the question explicitly rules out - and is MSCA-IF, failing the scheme filter too; 849229 CQWLED likewise guides 'chemistry and shape' of its nanocrystals, never opposes itself to lenses or reflectors (its foils are total internal reflection and EQE), and its 'layers' are the emitter superlattices rather than engineered surroundings. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the current question text): 657434 PhoLED (MSCA-IF-EF-ST) satisfies the textual ask outright and ranks dense 1 / hybrid 1 - 'integrating novel optical nanostructures and emitters, such as colloidal quantum dots or nanophosphors ... preparation and processing strategies, based on surface textures and colloidal scatterers, to attain large area optical nanostructures ... precise control on the intensity, angular distribution and color quality of light emission' - and it fails the ERC-STG filter, so dropping the filter changes the answer. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records what a project does with light emission; the filter alone leaves 10 candidates. TERM-STYLE paraphrase: the question uses 'tint', 'beam spread', 'low-energy lamps', 'stacked layers', 'patterned surfaces', 'resonant cavities' and avoids the gold's distinctive vocabulary (nanophosphor, LED, photonic, solid-state lighting, chromaticity, directionality, spectral, angular, integrated photonic systems). Unscoped on the current wording the lexical condition did NOT return 715832 in its top-10 (lexical rank 1 was 896410 OPAN) while dense ranked it 2, hybrid 3 and hybrid_rerank 2. Scoped lexical rank 1 is uninformative because the scope holds only 10 projects, so every survivor ranks in every condition.

text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is to study working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. NeWMaBIL records magnetoencephalography (MEG) from young and old adult bilinguals to test whether bilingualism works as a cognitive reserve for working-memory control, and reports that ageing reduces the attentional and working memory abilities while bilingual proficiency shows no reliable relation with the neural oscillatory modulation. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.
notes: Scope wording: 'whose stated aim is to study working memory' matches the filter's topic clause (objective or title), and deliberately excludes fellowships that merely ran a working-memory task while reporting - 655423 NIBSAD (stated aim: 'visuospatial attention and cognitive control processes'; tDCS working-memory task on eighteen healthy elderly in its report) and 844246 AGEING PLASTICITY (stated aim: prefrontal plasticity and resilience against cognitive ageing; retro-cue working memory task in its report) are out of scope by the question's own words. Filter: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (covers MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, MSCA-IF-GF; no MSCA-PF scheme exists in this corpus) AND working memory in objective or title; 18 survivors, inside the 5-20 filter-synthesize window. The runtime scoped path can only filter the structural half (fundingScheme); the topical half falls to retrieval, which is how the question is worded. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE over all 18 survivors (S<=20), not pooled; the scoped pooled search was run only for retrievability and the rank matrix (14 distinct projects returned). IN: 657255 NeWMaBIL - title states working memory control in aged bilinguals, MEG in young vs old adults, cognitive reserve in ageing; 749084 Motivageing - objective states the aim as enhancement of working memory capacity in healthy older adults and Parkinson's patients; 843158 COMEDM - title states decision-making and working memory in health and old age, extended to healthy older adults. OUT: 655374 ACCESS2WM (MEG, prior brain states and access to WM, healthy volunteers, no ageing); 700031 MORE-or-LESS (WM in mental arithmetic, children and adults); 703456 BrainCrossTalk (attention/inhibition oscillations; the single ageing token is a motivational aside, 'in pathological ageing'); 705630 PreMotive (MPFC-DLPFC interaction, EEG-fMRI); 705887 PtoACons (visual consciousness); 707141 MMPCURSRT (rehearsal in 210 children aged 6-10); 707312 GENEVA (DAT1/COMT genetics, attentional control and WM capacity); 753296 StressPFCog (glucocorticoid receptor, chronic stress, mice); 835767 InstrAct (instruction following); 838203 NumBraInf (number processing in infants; grant terminated after 17 days); 888270 SERWOM (serotonergic regulation of WM, mice); 892772 PIANISM (serotonin modulation of PFC circuits, mice); 893275 RootsofWorkingMemory (monkeys, apes, humans); 898460 PFCmap (mouse PFC circuit development); 101030415 ReWoMeN (deep-neural-network modelling of WM recall). Discrimination (filter load-bearing): projects that satisfy the textual ask but fail the scheme filter - 636458 CogSoCoAGE (ERC-STG, intervention to enhance social communication in older adults, working memory named as the executive component), 734718 CoBeN (MSCA-RISE - an MSCA scheme that is not an individual fellowship: visual working memory tasks in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's groups vs healthy controls). Both were surfaced by the unscoped pooled search on the question text. Non-embedding sweep over the survivors: regexp over objective + all report fields for (ageing|older adult|elderly|old age|age-related) returned exactly 657255, 703456, 749084, 843158; 703456's only hit is the aside quoted above. term_style exact-term: 'working memory', 'ageing', 'older adults' are the corpus's own words in all three gold texts, and lexical ranks all three inside the scoped top-5 (COMEDM 1, Motivageing 2, NeWMaBIL 5).

text: Among the MSCA-funded projects classified under inclusive education or special education, which ones collected their research data directly from large numbers of school students themselves, and how did their research designs differ?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle IN ('inclusive education','special education') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the six survivors did: IE2 (660607) and INCLUDed (101030992). IE2 ran its data collection inside schools - 'More than one thousand students across 35 classrooms took part, 25 teachers, administrators and district leaders' in Southern California, with data from two further European countries added during the first 24 months - and analysed it by combining advanced social network analysis with ethnographic methods to examine social interactions, friendships and peer relationships, with an emphasis on students identified as having special educational needs; its deliverables include a social network analysis toolkit for practitioners. INCLUDed collected data from a large nationally representative sample of 14-year-old lower-secondary students in Italy in order to develop, adapt and validate multifaceted measurement instruments for intercultural competence (IC) and for classroom cultural diversity climate (CCDC), the latter 'based on student perceptions of their learning environments', and then examined which culturally inclusive teaching approaches went with stronger IC. The designs differ in kind: IE2 is a school-based mixed network-and-ethnography study whose output is a practitioner toolkit, while INCLUDed is a large-scale quantitative instrument-development study whose output is validated measures plus evidence on teaching strategies.
notes: FILTER: purely structural - euroSciVoc leaf membership crossed with fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%'; unchanged since the first draft. Both leaves pass the one-reading check: SELECT DISTINCT euroSciVocPath, euroSciVocTitle, COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%inclusive education%' OR euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%special education%' GROUP BY 1,2 returns exactly two rows, 'social sciences/educational sciences/inclusive education' (10 projects) and 'social sciences/educational sciences/special education' (10), each a leaf, so title reading = subtree reading. Union of the two leaves is 19 projects (660607 carries both tags); crossing with MSCA leaves 6 survivors. No text/topic predicate anywhere in filter_sql. TEXTUAL PREDICATE: the project's own research data were collected directly from school students, in large numbers. Each conjunct is stated in both gold texts. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=6, every survivor read incl. workPerformed/finalResults): 660607 IE2 IN - 'Data collection from schools in Southern California has been completed. More than one thousand students across 35 classrooms took part, 25 teachers, administrators and district leaders'; 'data from two additional European countries have been collected during the first 24 months'. 101030992 INCLUDed IN - 'collected data from a large representative sample of lower-secondary students'; instrument for classroom cultural diversity climate 'based on student perceptions of their learning environments'; sample described in the objective as 'a large nationally representative sample of young people (14-year-olds) in a European country (i.e. Italy)'. 747083 MedLitRefYouth OUT - participants are not school students and are not numerous: '56 unaccompanied refugee children were interviewed', recruited 'By working with NGOs, volunteers and municipalities' in Italy and Sweden. 777720 CybSPEED OUT - no data collected from students: 'The grounds for sound experimental research have been laid, with some experiments already under way'; outputs are a theoretical framework, CPS models and Lattice Computing methods. 845783 ASSESSnet OUT - 'The data was principally collected by means of an online questionnaire and interviews with teachers involved in VM'; respondents are tertiary-level teachers. 101008184 xFORMAL OUT - work performed is scenario identification, a pathway editor, game mockups and feasibility tests of trails; no student data collection at all. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the current question text) surfaced text-satisfying projects that fail the filter: 101018401 INCLUSION (ERC-ADG, euroSciVoc political economy|human migrations - 'We launched the Mitigation Study in the 2021-2022 academic year, covering over 20,000 students from 65 middle schools in Diyarbakir, Turkey ... collecting data from students via tablets'), 101004653 Inclusion4Schools (CSA, democracy|ethnology - 'A comprehensive survey was carried out ... targeting 1,358 schools'), 749068 GENSEG (MSCA fellowship, no inclusive/special-education tag - 'Using secondary data of 2235 adolescents from SOEP'). So the filter is load-bearing. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records who a project's data came from or how its design was built; the filter alone returns six projects of which four are off-question. SCOPED RANKS (k=10, scope 6, current text): 101030992 lexical 1 / dense 1 / hybrid 1 / rerank 1; 660607 lexical 2 / dense 2 / hybrid 2 / rerank 2 - both gold top-2 in every condition, ahead of all four rejects. TERM_STYLE paraphrase: the textual half uses none of the gold texts' distinctive vocabulary ('social network analysis', 'friendship networks', 'special educational needs', 'intercultural competence', 'classroom cultural diversity climate', 'nationally representative sample'); the only verbatim overlap ('inclusive education' in IE2's title) sits in the scope half.

text: How many H2020 projects does CORDIS classify with a nature of crisis response, and when did the earliest of them start?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(startDate) AS earliest_start FROM project WHERE nature = 'crisisResponse'
reference_answer: CORDIS tags 90 H2020 projects with a nature of crisisResponse - its crisis-response category, one of three undocumented values alongside crisisPreparedness and crisisRecovery. The earliest of these 90 started on 2020-02-13.
notes: Value-grounded on project.nature: schema_docs states the column is null in 34,814 rows and otherwise holds crisisPreparedness|crisisRecovery|crisisResponse, explicitly flagged as 'values not in codebook' - the exact camelCase literal 'crisisResponse' cannot be guessed from the natural-language question.

text: Among ERC-funded Horizon 2020 projects, what is the average project duration in months for each ERC grant type - Starting (ERC-STG), Consolidator (ERC-COG), Advanced (ERC-ADG), and Proof of Concept (ERC-POC)?
gold_sql: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('month', startDate, endDate)), 2) AS avg_months FROM project WHERE fundingScheme IN ('ERC-STG', 'ERC-COG', 'ERC-ADG', 'ERC-POC') GROUP BY fundingScheme ORDER BY fundingScheme
reference_answer: ERC Proof of Concept (ERC-POC) projects run much shorter than the three main ERC grant types: ERC-POC averages 17.96 months, while ERC-ADG averages 67.46 months, ERC-COG averages 68.02 months, and ERC-STG averages 67.48 months.
notes: FIX (judge ruling, sql-s15, AMBIGUOUS-READING, UPHELD/HIGH): question text now names each fundingScheme code explicitly in parentheses so 'Proof of Concept' cannot be defensibly read to include the distinct ERC-POC-LS (lump-sum) code. gold_sql and reference_answer are unchanged (option a).

text: How many Horizon 2020 projects have at least one participating organization based in Italy?

reference_answer: 7,899 projects have at least one organization based in Italy (IT).
notes: Grain trap: organization is one row per project-organization participation (178,932 rows), so COUNT(*) after filtering country='IT' counts participations, not projects. Wrong query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM organization WHERE country='IT' -> 17243. Gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) ... -> 7899.

text: Which project's beta authentication app - designed to eliminate the need for passwords and CAPTCHAs by turning a phone into a universal security token - was tested by 12,000 users on Bluetooth proximity detection and keystroke-based behaviometrics?
reference_answer: Excalibur 2.0 (Excalibur Cloud Password Manager) is the project. It is designed to eliminate the need for passwords, logins, CAPTCHAs and verification emails, using a proprietary distributed cryptographic scheme so a phone acts as a universal security token that projects a strongly authenticated state to any device. Its Phase 1 feasibility study beta-tested this platform with 12,000 testers, exercising proximity detection based on Bluetooth and behaviometrics based on keystroke analysis (alongside a virtual browser / browser-sandboxing component).

text: International rules for use of the oceans were written for traditional shipping and state conduct. What common gap do research projects find between those older rules and situations such as cargo vessels with no human crew, military activity that stays just below the threshold of open warfare, and the past absence of any regime to protect biodiversity on the high seas?
reference_answer: The gap is the same in each case: the legal framework for ocean governance was built around crewed ships, formally declared war, and few claims on marine life outside national waters, and modern developments break those assumptions. P-ADMIRAL found that international law has no settled category for a cargo vessel that operates with no human crew at all - the Yara Birkeland - leaving liability, safety and compliance rules unclear for its automated operation. LOSFARE studied how States have used force or coercion against foreign shipping in busy straits (including the Kerch Strait and Strait of Hormuz incidents) in ways that stay below the threshold of open warfare, so the existing rules on navigation rights give decision-makers no clear roadmap for these hybrid-warfare incidents. MARIPOLDATA traced the 2018-2023 negotiation of a new binding treaty (BBNJ) under UNCLOS, undertaken precisely because the high seas had no dedicated regime protecting marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction; the project built a public database (MARIPOLDATAbase) cataloguing the entire negotiation.

text: Among the SME Instrument funded projects on serious games and game-based learning for education and training, which project pairs an immersive headset with an online training platform so that clinicians can safely rehearse on simulated patients instead of real ones?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%serious game%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%game-based learning%') AND (p.objective ILIKE '%learn%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%educat%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%training%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%'

reference_answer: The abcdeSIM-VR project (VirtualMedSchool, grant 781138) pairs a Virtual Reality headset with a web-based simulation platform that includes a serious game: the medical or health trainee wears the headset and performs on virtual patients in real-time under different clinical settings, without posing risk to real patients.
notes: Filter = SME Instrument (fundingScheme LIKE 'SME%') AND objective mentions serious game/game-based learning AND a learn/educat/training co-term. Survivors (3): 684657 TheCityGame pilot, 718990 LINGOKIDS, 781138 abcdeSIM-VR. Only 781138 has VR headset + web platform for medical training; other two are unrelated (language learning app, CSR sustainability app).

text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects working on ultrasound, which ones use the ultrasound waves themselves to trigger a therapeutic effect, such as releasing a drug or modulating brain activity, rather than only using ultrasound for imaging?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath = 'natural sciences/physical sciences/acoustics/ultrasound' AND p.fundingScheme='ERC-STG'

reference_answer: Of the 10 ERC Starting Grant projects tagged under the euroSciVoc ultrasound leaf, three use the ultrasound energy itself to produce a therapeutic effect rather than only to image or track. BONDS embeds alginate microparticles designed to respond to ultrasound by releasing a plasmid-DNA payload (pPDGF) on demand, timing angiogenic gene delivery to guide diabetic-foot-ulcer wound healing. BUBBLE CURE vibrates vancomycin-decorated targeted microbubbles with ultrasound to both image and physically reduce cardiac-device-associated bacterial biofilms, reporting roughly a 20% biofilm reduction from ultrasound-triggered microbubble application. HelpUS built a focused-ultrasound neurostimulation system to non-invasively modulate deep brain activity (alongside ultrasound imaging), aiming to establish causal links between brain circuits and empathy-related decision making; the other seven survivors (ROBOTAR, ExtreFlow, MicroParticleControl, DYNA-MIC, L-SID, MUSE, GUTSY) use ultrasound only for imaging, tracking, sensing, or as a general acoustic process tool.
notes: Filter redesigned onto euroSciVoc ultrasound leaf (single-row one-reading check) x fundingScheme=ERC-STG, since objective/title ILIKE is a banned structured-filter column. 10 survivors, 3 IN on the distinction: ultrasound as active therapeutic trigger vs. imaging tool.
